text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-7654 — Postgres connection pool high on reddb-prod (95% used). Auto-page to rotation.

tina: acked. i'm on it. starting triage — checking active connections and application error rates.

pagerduty-bot: Alert acknowledged by tina (on-call). Escalation timer paused.

raj: seeing a rapid spike from jobs-worker replicas, lots of short txns. redis is returning 504s intermittently so app falls back to DB. looks like a cache miss storm -> connection stampede.

anya: confirming customer impact: increased 502/503 errors on write-heavy endpoints (billing, invoices). Frontend SLOs are slipping.

ken: paging CS to let them know we may throttle background jobs briefly. cc @support-team.

raj: quick checks:
```
-- active connections
SELECT pid, usename, application_name, state, query_start, now()-query_start as age FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle' ORDER BY age DESC LIMIT 10;
```
shows hundreds of connections with <1s queries but high churn. pgbouncer pools nearly saturated.

tina: ok. mitigation plan: 1) pause jobs-worker cron dispatch (short-term), 2) enable pgbouncer transaction pooling for the worker pool, 3) temporary rate-limit inbound write routes. doing step 1 now.

jake: how to pause? kubectl scale? which job controller?

raj: jobs-runner is a k8s CronJob + horizontal job runner. run: `kubectl -n prod scale deploy jobs-dispatcher --replicas=0` — will stop new jobs without killing currently running. also increase pgbouncer max_client_conn by 100 to buy time.

tina: executing scale now. `kubectl -n prod scale deploy jobs-dispatcher --replicas=0`

sre-runbot: deploy triggered: scale deployment jobs-dispatcher -> 0 (by tina). Notified deployment controller.

anya: seeing immediate drop in new DB connections after ~8s. frontend error rate still high but trending down.

raj: bumping pgbouncer config (one-off) on pool-proxy:
```
[pgbouncer]
max_client_conn = 3000
default_pool_size = 80
```
reloaded pgbouncer on pool-proxy-1.

ken: CS updated: told them we're pausing job dispatch, increasing pool, and may apply temporary rate limits. they asked about ETA — ~15-30m.

tina: enabling emergency rate-limit for /api/v1/invoices and /api/v1/billing via edge-proxy: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/limits -d '{"routes": ["/api/v1/invoices","/api/v1/billing"], "rate": "20rps"}'`

raj: DB metrics: active connections down 40% in last 30s, wait queue latency falling. redis 504s still seen but less frequent. looks like the cache warmup is ongoing.

jake: any schema-locks or long-running queries?

raj: no heavy locks. majority are fast `INSERT INTO job_runs ...` churn. they saturate max_backends quickly.

anya: customer-impact scoreboard: 1) billing APIs degraded (partial), 2) background billing jobs delayed, 3) some customers saw invoice generation failures (retrying). Raised internal incident page to S-2.

tina: good catch. starting post-mortem notes and preserving logs: `pg_dump` not needed, capturing `pg_stat_activity` and pgbouncer logs.

raj: manual short-term rollback options: 1) flip feature-flag to reduce write fanout (feature: invoice_notify_batch=false) 2) route worker traffic to secondary DB (read-only), not ideal for writes.

tina: i'm toggling FF to throttle write fanout for the next 20m. informing developers.

sre-runbot: feature-flag toggle recorded by tina.

pagerduty-bot: PD-7654: escalation to secondary contact scheduled at +30m if unresolved.

ken: telemetry shows error budget getting close. recommend follow-up: schedule a Dedicated capacity review for DB pool defaults and pgbouncer tuning.

jake: prepping handoff — i can cover next 30m while tina writes up the incident summary. what else needs action?

raj: follow-ups: 1) investigate root cause of redis 504s (network/redis-client timeouts), 2) tune job-runner backoff/retry config to avoid stampedes, 3) add circuit-breaker in app to fallback more gracefully.

tina: drafting brief for oncall handoff: current status = mitigated (jobs paused, pgbouncer bumped, rate limits in place, ff toggled). ongoing: cache warmup + redis probe. next steps for jake: monitor pg wait queue and frontend 5xxs, coordinate with infra on redis probe.

jake: ack. i'll monitor and escalate if >10% 5xx persists. keeping PD alerts unmuted for DB high-connections.

anya: i'll update customers affected and record incident in tracker.

ken: leaving note for SRE playbook addition: auto-pause job-dispatcher runbook snippet.

tina: handing off to jake — i'm OOO for next 40m but reachable if needed. thanks all. :thumbsup:

jake: taking over. marking thread as in-progress and will post resolution timeline when stable.

pagerduty-bot: PD-7654 acknowledged by jake.

sre-runbot: incident notes saved to /incidents/PD-7654/summary.md (auto-draft).

tina: resolved? we'll close after 1 hour of stable metrics.

jake: agreed. will close when 5xx < 1% for 30m and DB wait queue normal.

ken: good work. postmortem owners: raj + tina. i'll add action items.

-- end of thread --
